correctness.rationale: For a Dyck prefix ending at i and Dyck suffix starting after j with j≤i, their overlapping height constraints force total balance H=0, and the union covers a nonnegative path. Thus non-Dyck words have separated maximal Dyck ends and a nonempty invariant core: extending past a maximal end would require a Dyck end of the core, since appending a balanced nonnegative excursion cannot restore a still-positive height to zero. Each move cuts off complete primitive factors at one end; for a Dyck word this is a single heap, and otherwise the two end counts are independent Nim heaps. The intersection with (ab)*b(ab)* really is the equal-count language, proving nonregularity. The unique decomposition gives q=(1−p)^2/(1−2z)−(1−p); the common high bits in k and k xor g yield the geometric residue-block denominator. At z=1/2, the fixed-count pair has leading pole 2^(−k−l−2)/(1−2z), and these limiting masses sum to one. The loss series expands as 1/[3(1−2z)]+(4√2/9)(1−2z)^(-1/2)+constant+O(√(1−2z)); at −1/2 only a weaker square-root term occurs. Since |p(z)|≤1/2 on the closed convergence disk, there are no competing denominator zeros there. Coefficient transfer gives the stated probability and correction. Read the supplied scripts and saved output without executing: the finite checking report overcounts the tested residue identities, since verify_series.py lines 67–78 skips the assertion for g=8,…,15 (2M=32>N//2=30); only eight reach it. This is nonessential corroboration, not a defect in the all-length proof. Exact replay locators for the mathematical checks are RESULT.md lines 62–95 and the residue loop in verify_series.py.
